title: feat(auth): add under-16 family guidance flow
body:
Closes #3532

## Summary
This PR adds the client-side under-16 family guidance flow.

It is intentionally scoped to mobile UX only:
- a new welcome-screen entry point
- a deep-linkable `/account-review` flow
- an under-13 parent-or-guardian email path
- a 13-15 parental consent path that tells families to record the video outside the app and email it to `support@divine.video`

This PR does **not** add moderation backend wiring, private in-app video submission, or any DM-based consent-video flow.

## What Changed
- adds a new welcome CTA: `Not 16 yet? That's OK. Here's what you can do.`
- adds a public `account-review` route family that works from welcome or a moderation deep link later
- adds a shared explainer screen about regional rules and Divine's family-guidance approach
- adds an under-13 screen that directs parents or guardians to email `support@divine.video`
- adds a 13-15 screen that explains the parental consent video requirements and makes the path explicitly email-only
- adds deep-link parsing for `https://divine.video/account-review?source=...`
- adds focused router, deep-link, and widget tests for the new flow

## Product Boundaries In This PR
- Under 13: parent or guardian must email support. No in-app workaround.
- Age 13 to 15: the parental consent video must be recorded outside the app and emailed to support.
- Under no circumstances should a parental consent video be posted on Divine.
- DM can be wired later for moderation/support communication, but this PR does not claim that DM is a safe path for sending the video itself.

## Not Included
- moderation case creation or server state
- restricted-account enforcement from backend signals
- private media upload or encrypted video attachment support
- moderator tooling in other repos

## Main Files
- `mobile/lib/screens/auth/welcome_screen.dart`
- `mobile/lib/screens/minor_account_review_screen.dart`
- `mobile/lib/screens/minor_account_review_under13_support_screen.dart`
- `mobile/lib/screens/minor_account_review_parent_consent_screen.dart`
- `mobile/lib/router/app_router.dart`
- `mobile/lib/services/deep_link_service.dart`
- `mobile/lib/main.dart`
- `mobile/lib/l10n/app_en.arb`

## Verification
From `mobile/`:
- `flutter test --no-pub test/screens/minor_account_review_screen_test.dart test/screens/welcome_screen_test.dart test/router/login_flow_redirect_test.dart test/router/route_normalization_test.dart test/services/deep_link_service_test.dart test/router/universal_link_resolver_test.dart`
- `flutter analyze lib/screens/minor_account_review_parent_consent_screen.dart lib/screens/minor_account_review_screen.dart lib/screens/minor_account_review_under13_support_screen.dart lib/screens/auth/welcome_screen.dart lib/router/app_router.dart lib/services/deep_link_service.dart test/screens/minor_account_review_screen_test.dart test/screens/welcome_screen_test.dart`

## Follow-Up
The next phase, in other repos, is a real private submission system if we still want one:
- backend upload contract
- private storage and moderator review tools
- a separate capture/upload path with no draft save and no publish flow

title: fix(dm): split optimistic into pendingOptimistic slice (#4193)
body:
## Summary

- Fixes #4193 — sent DMs were invisible in the live conversation until app restart on a freshly-searched user.
- Root cause: `_onMessageSent`'s in-memory optimistic and `_onStarted`'s watch-stream-driven projection both wrote to `state.messages`. A watch tick landing between the optimistic emit and the persistence transaction commit (the empty first tick on a fresh conversation, or any tick on a slow Keycast RPC signer) clobbered the bubble.
- Fix: move the in-flight optimistic into a new `state.pendingOptimistic` map keyed by `pendingId`. The watch path keeps replacing `state.messages` verbatim; `_onMessageSent` never touches that slice. A new `state.displayedMessages` getter merges the two for the UI.

## How the race fires (pre-fix)

1. User opens conversation → `BlocProvider` creates `ConversationBloc` with `..add(ConversationStarted())`.
2. `_onStarted` emits `(loading, [])`, then `await markConversationAsRead`, then `emit.forEach(watchMessages, …)` subscribes — `restartable()` bucket.
3. User taps send fast (typical when someone just searched a contact to message).
4. `_onMessageSent` runs in the `sequential()` bucket — concurrent with `_onStarted` — and emits `state.copyWith(messages: [optimistic, ...state.messages])`.
5. drift's `query.watch()` fires its initial tick: `[]` (no rows yet for a fresh conversation).
6. `emit.forEach.onData` replaces `state.messages` with `[]`. **Optimistic gone.**
7. `sendMessage` finishes → transaction commits → drift fires → `[persisted]` emitted. But on slow signers (Keycast RPC) or slow networks the gap between (5) and (7) is seconds. The user "observes" during that gap and sees an empty conversation.
8. Restart → fresh bloc → watch's first tick is `[persisted]` → user sees the message.

## Fix

```
state.messages           ← persisted truth, replaced verbatim by every watchMessages tick
state.pendingOptimistic  ← in-flight optimistic, keyed by pendingId, owned only by _onMessageSent
state.displayedMessages  ← getter; merges the two, preferring persisted on id collision
```

Strip rules:
- **sent / sentPartial**: remove the matching pending key. The watch tick brings the persisted row microseconds later (drift fires on transaction commit).
- **failed**: remove the matching pending key. `state.messages` stays untouched (no DB write happened).

Same `_onMessageSent` exception, retry, partial-delivery, and group-send shapes — only the slice that holds the optimistic moves. The brainstorm doc included in this PR maps the design 1:1 to #3909's planned `Rx.combineLatest2(watchMessages, watchOutgoing)` projection, so this slice is easy to retire when that lands.

## Files

- `mobile/lib/blocs/dm/conversation/conversation_state.dart` — new `pendingOptimistic` field, `displayedMessages` getter, `copyWith` parameter.
- `mobile/lib/blocs/dm/conversation/conversation_bloc.dart` — `_onMessageSent` writes / strips `pendingOptimistic`; `_onStarted` unchanged.
- `mobile/lib/screens/inbox/conversation/conversation_view.dart` — `_ConversationContent` selector reads `state.displayedMessages`.
- `mobile/test/blocs/dm/conversation/conversation_bloc_test.dart` — state-shape + projection tests, **new race-pinning regression test driving a `StreamController<List<DmMessage>>`**, and migrated assertions on the existing send / fail / partial / group / retry / pendingId-uniqueness tests.
- `mobile/test/screens/inbox/conversation/conversation_view_test.dart` — new test: `MessageBubble` renders when only `pendingOptimistic` is populated.
- `mobile/docs/brainstorm/2026-05-10-issue4193-dm-optimistic-watch-race-brainstorm.md` — design alternatives and rationale.

## Test plan

Automated:
- [x] `dart format` — clean.
- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — clean.
- [x] `flutter test test/blocs/dm test/screens/inbox` — **324 / 324 passing**.

Tightened existing tests + added new ones:
- `conversation_bloc_test.dart`:
  - **NEW** `'optimistic survives a watchMessages tick that arrives mid-send (regression for #4193)'` — drives a real `StreamController<List<DmMessage>>`, pushes an empty tick during the awaited `sendMessage`, asserts `displayedMessages.length == 1` while `sendStatus == sending`. Pre-fix this would have observed `displayedMessages.isEmpty` at that frame.
  - **NEW** `'pendingOptimistic defaults to empty and participates in equality'` and `'displayedMessages projection'` group (4 tests covering empty fast-path, ordering, collision-with-persisted, unmodifiable view).
  - Migrated every send-side `s.messages.length` assertion to `s.displayedMessages.length` (user-visible) plus `s.pendingOptimistic` (in-flight tracking) so the two slices are pinned independently.
  - Rewrote the pendingId-uniqueness test to assert the strip semantics directly (`Map.remove(pendingId)`) using a seeded sibling pending — a cleaner contract than the prior list-walk-based scenario.
- `conversation_view_test.dart`:
  - **NEW** `'renders MessageBubble when only pendingOptimistic is populated (regression for #4193)'` — pumps a state with empty `messages` + non-empty `pendingOptimistic`, asserts `MessageBubble` is mounted and `EmptyConversation` is not.

Manual verification (please confirm during review):
- [ ] Search a fresh user via the inbox FAB on Android. Type a message. Tap send. Confirm the optimistic bubble appears immediately and stays visible.
- [ ] Verify the persisted row remains after pop + re-enter.
- [ ] Toggle airplane mode mid-send to force a failure → SnackBar shows, optimistic disappears, Retry works (existing #3908 path, no regression).

## What's deferred

- The principled fix from #3909 — `Rx.combineLatest2(watchMessages, watchOutgoing)` at the repository layer with status-aware bubble UI — is the long-term destination. This PR is bug-scoped, and the slice it introduces maps 1:1 to the `pending` projection that #3909 will produce; switching is mechanical when the merged stream lands.

## Investigation + brainstorm

The full investigation (5-Whys, layer trace, alternative approaches, regression risk) was captured via `/investigate` and `/brainstorm` immediately before this PR. The brainstorm doc lives at `mobile/docs/brainstorm/2026-05-10-issue4193-dm-optimistic-watch-race-brainstorm.md`.

title: perf(rebuilds): swap context.watch for context.select on three hot widgets
body:
## Description

`context.watch<X>()` triggers a rebuild whenever any field of `X.state`
changes, even when the widget only reads one or two of them. This PR
replaces three such call sites with `context.select` projections so each
widget rebuilds only when the data it actually consumes changes.

### `profile_videos_grid.dart`

The highest-impact site — `BackgroundPublishState` emits on every upload
progress tick, and the previous `context.watch` made the entire profile
videos grid rebuild every tick (de-duplication loop, layout, etc.) even
though it only cares about the *shape* of the active upload list.

- Project state to `List<({String draftId, String? title, String? thumbnailPath})>`
  via `context.select`. Progress is intentionally excluded so progress
  ticks no longer rebuild the grid.
- ` _VideoGridUploadingTile` now subscribes to its own upload's progress
  via `context.select<BackgroundPublishBloc, double>(...)`, so only the
  affected tile rebuilds when its progress advances.

### `video_editor_draw_item_indicator.dart`

One-line swap — only reads `selectedTool` from a 7-field state. Now
rebuilds only when the selected tool changes (was also rebuilding on
undo/redo, color, and stroke-width changes).

### `profile_header_widget.dart`

Project `MyProfileBloc` state to `(profile, isInitialOrLoading)`. The
header now ignores `isFresh` / `extractedUsername` / `verifiedClaims` /
error-variant transitions that don't affect what it renders.

**Related Issue:** Closes #3605

title: feat(dm): auto-sweep self-wrap-failed outgoing_dms via foreground retry service
body:
## Description

Closes #4124. Adds an `OutgoingDmRetryService` that sweeps the durable
`outgoing_dms` queue on every app-foreground transition and re-publishes
the missing self-wrap for any row in `recipient: sent / self: failed`
state via the `recoverSelfWrap` primitive landed in PR #4106.

Today that primitive is only invoked when the user manually taps the
partial-delivery SnackBar's Retry action. The SnackBar is ephemeral, so
dismissed taps and app-killed sessions leave self-wrap-failed rows
durably broken — silently breaking sender cross-device sync, the
*entire purpose* of NIP-17 self-wrapping.

The service mirrors `PendingActionService` one-for-one — same precedent
epic #3912 explicitly cites. It ships with a broad-shaped strategy
table but only the self-wrap-only entry wired today; rows in
`recipient: failed` state are enumerated and counted in logs to inform
the `recoverFullSend` follow-up (#4240).

**Related Issue:** Closes #4124. Follow-up: #4240. Parent epic: #3912.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

## Changes

**`OutgoingDmRetryService` (`mobile/lib/services/outgoing_dm_retry_service.dart`)**
- New service. Subscribes to `appForegroundProvider`. On each foreground
  transition to `true`, runs one sweep over `getRetryableForOwner`.
- Per-row backoff via `OutgoingDmRetryConfig` — defaults match
  `PendingActionRetryConfig` verbatim (5 retries, 2s → 5min, 2× backoff).
  Backoff state is durable across app kill (the DAO already writes
  `last_attempt_at` on every `markXxxWrapStatus` / `incrementRetry`).
- Re-entrancy guard: a sweep already in progress short-circuits the
  next trigger.
- Strategy dispatch:
  - **State A** (`recipient: sent / self: failed`) → `recoverSelfWrap`.
    `incrementRetry` is called only on a real publish failure so
    transient repo-not-ready states don't burn the retry budget.
  - **State B** (`recipient: failed`) → log-and-count only. Pinned via
    `verifyNever(recoverSelfWrap(rumorId: 'b'))` in the contract test.
- Error handling: `StateError` (repo not initialized) aborts the pass
  without bumping retry; `ArgumentError` (row missing / foreign owner)
  is terminal-skip; other throws bump retry and continue.

**`outgoingDmRetryServiceProvider` (`mobile/lib/providers/app_providers.dart`)**
- New `@Riverpod(keepAlive: true)` factory. Returns null when
  `userPubkey` is null OR when `isNostrReadyProvider` is false (Pattern A
  from `state_management.md` — gates dependents on readiness instead of
  catching `StateError` inside the service).
- Bridges the synchronous `appForegroundProvider` notifier into a
  `Stream<bool>` via `ref.listen(..., fireImmediately: true)` plus a
  `StreamController`, so the service contract stays free of Riverpod
  types and is easy to drive from unit tests.

**`main.dart`**
- Single `ref.watch(outgoingDmRetryServiceProvider)` at app shell setup.
  The service has no UI consumer (it operates on the durable queue), so
  without an explicit read it would never be created.

**No DAO / repository / UI / BLoC / l10n / schema changes.** The DAO is
already retry-service-ready (`getRetryableForOwner({maxRetries})`,
`incrementRetry`, durable `last_attempt_at`, per-wrap error columns —
all from PR #3911).

## Test plan

Automated:
- [x] `dart format` — no changes.
- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — clean.
- [x] `mobile/test/services/outgoing_dm_retry_service_test.dart` — 21
      new tests, all passing. Covers initialize/dispose, dispatch by row
      state, per-row backoff (skip / proceed / fresh), error handling
      (`StateError` aborts pass, `ArgumentError` skips row, generic
      throw bumps retry), re-entrancy guard, account scope, and
      `OutgoingDmRetryConfig.backoffFor` math.
- [x] `mobile/test/services/pending_action_service_test.dart` — 42
      tests, no regression in the precedent service.
- [x] `mobile/test/blocs/dm/` — 146 tests, no regression in DM blocs.
- [x] `mobile/packages/dm_repository` — 219 tests, no regression in
      `recoverSelfWrap`'s contract.
- [x] `mobile/test/providers/dm_repository_provider_test.dart` — 3
      tests, no regression in the DM provider's gift-wrap subscription
      lifecycle.

Pinning contracts added:
- The sweep never invokes `sendMessage` / `sendGroupMessage` / any
  recipient-publishing path (`verifyNever` on each in the
  "never republishes recipient wraps" group).
- `recipient: failed` rows are visible to `getRetryableForOwner` but
  are NOT dispatched to `recoverSelfWrap`.
- `incrementRetry` is called once per real publish failure and never
  on `StateError`/`ArgumentError` (the abort/skip paths).
- A second `sweep()` call while one is already in progress
  short-circuits without re-entering the loop.

Manual verification (please confirm during review):
- [ ] Force a self-wrap publish failure on a 1:1 send (e.g. block the
      second `publishEvent` round in a debug build), then **dismiss**
      the SnackBar without tapping Retry. Background and re-foreground
      the app — the row should be recovered automatically and the
      `outgoing_dms` row should be gone.
- [ ] App-kill the app between the recipient publish and the self-wrap
      publish (debug build). Re-launch. The cold-start foreground
      transition should fire one sweep; if the recipient publish had
      landed, the row should be recovered. (Caveat: a row in
      `recipient: pending / self: pending` state — i.e., we don't yet
      know whether the recipient publish landed — is out of scope for
      this PR's filter; it's covered by #4240's follow-up.)
- [ ] On a long foreground session, observe the per-row backoff in
      logs: `skipped-backoff=N` should grow as the same row gets
      re-evaluated within its backoff window.

## Brainstorm + plan

The design rationale (why a foreground-only trigger; why the broad
service shape with only self-wrap-only recovery wired today; why
mirror `PendingActionService` instead of putting the loop inside
`DmRepository`) is captured in
`mobile/docs/brainstorm/2026-05-10-issue4124-outgoing-dm-auto-sweep-brainstorm.md`,
included in this PR.

title: fix(profile): adjust memCacheWidth calculation for profile-tab thumbnails
body:
Closes #4221



## Description

PR #4191 was merged with an unresolved review comment about thumbnail decoding performance — the very issue that PR was meant to optimize.

## Problem

#4191 introduced a hardcoded `memCacheWidth = 400` for profile tab thumbnails. In practice, the actual rendered tile width (in physical pixels) varies between **~160 and ~600 px** depending on device size and `devicePixelRatio`:

- On small / low-DPR devices: we decode **more pixels than the tile can show** → wasted RAM and CPU on every grid item.
- On large / high-DPR devices: we decode **fewer pixels than the tile shows** → upscaled, blurry thumbnails.

A single static value cannot satisfy both ends of the device spectrum.

## Fix

Compute `memCacheWidth` from the actual tile constraints at build time:

```dart
LayoutBuilder(
  builder: (context, constraints) {
    final dpr = MediaQuery.devicePixelRatioOf(context);
    final memCacheWidth = (constraints.maxWidth * dpr).round();
    return VineCachedImage(memCacheWidth: memCacheWidth, ...);
  },
)
```

This guarantees each device decodes thumbnails at exactly its required resolution — no waste, no upscaling.

## Notes

- `memCacheHeight` is intentionally left unset; setting both axes triggers `ResizeImagePolicy.fit` to pick the tighter axis, which causes portrait thumbnails to upscale under `BoxFit.cover`.
- A follow-up may bucket the computed width (e.g. nearest 32 px) to avoid re-decodes on window resize on web/desktop.

title: ci(codemagic): clean stale Xcode/SPM workspace state before iOS builds
body:
Closes #4236

## Summary

The Codemagic iOS archive step intermittently dies with:

> `** INTERNAL ERROR: Unable to load workspace 'Runner.xcworkspace' **`
> `Uncaught Exception: *** -[NSMutableArray insertObjects:atIndexes:]: count of array (53) differs from count of index set (52)`
> `IDESwiftPackageCore … sortedInsert(of:) … registerDependencyFileReferences …`

Root cause is a desynced `Runner.xcworkspace/xcshareddata/swiftpm/workspace-state.json` carried over within a single Codemagic build — the iOS workflow opens the workspace three times (`flutter build ios --config-only`, `pod install`, `flutter build ipa`), and Xcode 16's `IDESwiftPackageCore` occasionally trips on a stale SPM graph from the earlier opens.

## Fix

Add a shared `clean_ios_workspace_state` step that wipes:
- `$HOME/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData`
- `ios/Pods` and `ios/.symlinks`
- `ios/Runner.xcworkspace/xcuserdata`
- `ios/Runner.xcworkspace/xcshareddata/swiftpm`

…before each iOS workflow runs, so the archive step always sees a freshly-resolved SPM graph. Wired into `ios-build`, `ios-simulator-build`, and `e2e-smoke-ios`. `Podfile.lock` is intentionally left in place so pod resolution stays reproducible across CI runs.

## Test plan

- [ ] Run the `iOS Build` workflow on Codemagic from this branch and confirm the archive completes
- [ ] Re-run a few times — the failure was intermittent, so a single green run isn't proof
- [ ] `iOS Simulator Build` workflow still passes
- [ ] `E2E Smoke Tests (iOS)` workflow still passes

title: feat(video): show likers/reposters list when owner taps like/repost
body:
Closes #4173

## Summary
- Tapping Like or Repost on your own video used to toggle your own like/repost — meaningless on a video you authored. It now opens a full-screen list of the users who liked or reposted that video instead.
- Adds a new repository method on each engagement-tracking package (`likes_repository.fetchEventLikers`, `reposts_repository.fetchEventReposters`) that pulls reactor / reposter pubkeys directly from relays. Funnelcake's REST API only exposes aggregate engagement counts, so the lists have to come from a kind 7 / kind 6+16 relay query, deduped across `e` / `a` tags and with kind 5 deletions filtered out.
- New `VideoEngagementBloc` + `VideoEngagementListScreen` (Page/View) at `/video/:eventId/likers` and `/video/:eventId/reposters`, with an optional `?a=` query param for addressable Kind 30000+ events. The list reuses the existing `UserProfileTile` (without the follow CTA) for rendering.
- Threads `isOwnVideo` from the existing check in `VideoOverlayActionColumn` down into `LikeActionButton` and `RepostActionButton`. On the owner's own video, the tap navigates instead of dispatching the toggle event.

## Known limitations / follow-ups
- The lists are loaded once when the screen opens (single relay query, returns when EOSE fires). They don't subscribe for live updates of new likes / reposts that arrive while the screen is open. Pull-to-refresh re-runs the query. Eventually we'll want a live-subscription-backed list and pagination once it matters; this v1 ships the full list because most own-video engagement counts are small.
- Five new ARB keys (`videoEngagementLikersTitle` / `RepostersTitle` / `LikersEmpty` / `RepostersEmpty` / `LoadFailed`) are added in English and allowlisted in `arb_consistency_test.dart` so non-English locales fall back to English until the next translation pass — same pattern as the recent Edit / Report button additions.

## Test plan
- [ ] As the video author, tap the Like button on your own video → likers list opens; back returns to the feed; refresh re-queries.
- [ ] As the video author, tap the Repost button on your own video → reposters list opens; tapping a profile pushes their profile screen.
- [ ] As another user, tap Like on someone else's video → still toggles like (count flips, heart fills).
- [ ] As another user, tap Repost on someone else's video → still toggles repost.
- [ ] Empty-state copy renders when no one has liked / reposted yet.
- [ ] Failure state renders + retry works when the relay query fails.
- [ ] Both addressable (Kind 34236 with d-tag) and non-addressable target events work — the addressable id is forwarded as `?a=` and merged with the `e`-tag results.

- Adds a 3:1 banner image preview + upload UI on the profile setup screen, alongside a banner-scoped color picker.

title: fix(router): safe pop fallback so empty-stack back buttons land on home feed
body:
## Scope

This PR is **introduce-the-helper + migrate the dominant crash site**, plus a bundled CI fix. There are ~28 other `context.pop()` callers in `mobile/lib/screens` that are latent for the same crash class. They are not migrated here so this stays reviewable; follow-ups can sweep them once this lands.

## Summary

Fixes the dominant Crashlytics issue [`5c465b01...`](https://console.firebase.google.com/u/0/project/openvine-co/crashlytics/app/ios:co.openvine.app/issues/5c465b01bb5421f294ecca1adaaf440a?time=7d) — `Fatal Exception: FlutterError - GoError: There is nothing to pop` (928 events / 161 users in the last 7 days; 78% in profile flows; iOS 26).

**Root cause.** `KeyManagementScreen` is a top-level `GoRoute` (`/key-management`). When a caller navigates with `go` / `goNamed` / a deep link, the matched hierarchy collapses to `[/key-management]` and the AppBar's bare `onBackPressed: context.pop` throws on the next tap. PR #3941 (May 5) added a high-traffic entry point — `profile_setup_screen.dart`'s "view public key" link used `context.goNamed(KeyManagementScreen.routeName)`, which reset the back stack — explaining the recent 1.0.11 / 1.0.12 spike. The Apr 14 (1.0.8) regression is the older underlying weakness for any other empty-stack path (deep link, double-tap, etc.).

## Changes

Three concerns; calling them out separately for review:

**1. New helper (defense-in-depth, applies to all top-level routes)**
- `lib/extensions/safe_pop_extension.dart` — `context.safePop({String? fallback})`. Checks `canPop()` first; falls back to `defaultSafePopFallback` (`/home/0`) or a caller-supplied route instead of crashing.
- `key_management_screen.dart` — AppBar back button and post-import dismiss now use `context.safePop`.

**2. Proximate fix in profile-setup (separate behaviour change)**
- `profile_setup_screen.dart` L2222 — "view public key" link flips from `goNamed` to `pushNamed`. This is a deliberate behaviour change: `pushNamed` adds to the stack so the back arrow returns to the profile editor (preserving unsaved edits) instead of resetting. This is what PR #3941 intended; `goNamed` was the bug.
- `profile_setup_screen.dart` L417-429 — replaces an existing `try/catch (e) { context.pop() }` block with a `canPop()` guard. Same fallback semantics (go to `/profile/$npub` when authenticated, else `/home/0`); just stops using exception flow for control flow.

**3. Bundled CI fix — repo-wide preview-deploy break (helps the *next* PR after this merges, not this one)**
- `.github/workflows/mobile_pr_preview_deploy.yml` — pass `--commit-hash`/`--commit-message=$HEAD_SHA` explicitly to wrangler. Without these flags, `cloudflare/wrangler-action`'s `pages deploy` falls back to `git log -1` of the workflow's checkout — which on `workflow_run` is *main's* tip, not the PR head. Cloudflare's API has been rejecting main's current message — `Invalid commit message, it must be a valid UTF-8 string [code 8000111]` — apparently because wrangler 3.90.0 mojibakes the em-dashes in commit `0585d82e` (#4106) on Ubuntu runners. Every PR triggered after #4106 merged has been failing the deploy step (build is green; only the deploy and the comment that follows are broken). ASCII-only SHAs sidestep it.
  - **Important caveat:** GitHub runs `workflow_run` workflows from the **default branch's** copy of the YAML, so this change does *not* affect this PR's own deploy. Once this PR merges to main, all subsequent PRs will pick up the fix. Bundling here rather than separately because the change is one line and the rationale is the same investigation.

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter analyze` clean on the four touched files
- [x] New extension tests pass (6/6)
- [x] Existing `key_management_screen_test.dart` and `profile_setup_screen_test.dart` still pass (45/45)
- [ ] Manual: open app via deep link to `/key-management`, tap back → lands on home feed (no crash)
- [ ] Manual: edit profile → "view public key" → back → returns to edit profile (preserved stack)
- [ ] Post-merge verification: next PR triggered after merge should produce a fresh "Mobile PR Preview" comment instead of failing on `Invalid commit message`

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Sweep remaining ~28 `onBackPressed: context.pop` call sites (auth/nostr_connect, library, video_detail, other_profile, etc.) onto `context.safePop`.
- Consider making `DiVineAppBar`'s default back behaviour `safePop` so future top-level screens are protected by construction.
- Audit `mobile_web_production_deploy.yml` for the same `--commit-message` gap.

2. **PR 2 small batches** (`f04227270` … `d0d11bf3c`): translated

3. **PR 3 full passes** (`c36bd1c59`): translated the 39 keys that
   were missing or English-valued in every locale. Covers Video

   Reason Subtitles + Learn More (App Store compliance), Video

- **High confidence**: en, de, es, fr, it, nl, pt

title: build(ci): add macOS lane for iOS attestation RunnerTests
body:
Closes #4119. Follow-up to #3979.

## Summary

Adds a `runner-tests` job to `.github/workflows/mobile_ci.yaml` that runs the Swift `RunnerTests` suite from #3979 on `macos-14` so regressions in `NostrBridgeAttestationPolicy` or `FrameAttestingScriptMessageHandler.eventPayload` fail CI instead of relying on a contributor remembering to run `xcodebuild test` locally.

## Why

The Nostr bridge attestation work is a security-sensitive boundary. The two types this PR gates are:

- `NostrBridgeAttestationPolicy` — single-instance attach/detach state machine that prevents the per-frame attestation handler from being silently dropped or swapped.
- `FrameAttestingScriptMessageHandler.eventPayload` — pinned contract that the Dart-bound payload contains exactly `{message, isMainFrame}` and never leaks origin host/port/scheme upward.

Without a CI lane these tests are honor-system. This PR makes them required.

## What changed

`.github/workflows/mobile_ci.yaml`:

- New `runner-tests` job on `macos-14` with Xcode `15.4` pinned via `maxim-lobanov/setup-xcode@v1`. Flutter `3.41.9` matches the existing Ubuntu jobs verbatim.
- Steps: `flutter precache --ios` → `flutter pub get` → `flutter build ios --config-only --no-codesign` (writes `Generated.xcconfig` so the Podfile resolves `FLUTTER_ROOT`) → CocoaPods cache keyed on `Podfile.lock` → `pod install` → `xcodebuild test -only-testing:RunnerTests` against an iPhone 15 simulator.
- Code signing is disabled (`CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`, `CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO`) — simulator unit tests don't need a profile.
- On failure the `.xcresult` bundle is uploaded as an artifact for triage.
- `mobile-ci` aggregator now `needs: runner-tests` and exits non-zero if it fails, so the lane becomes transitively required by branch protection without any branch-protection rule change.

No `paths:` filter — runs on every PR to `main`, matching the existing workflow's convention. The cost (~5–7 macOS minutes per PR) is acceptable for a security-critical lane.

## Test plan

- [ ] First run on this PR is green; `runner-tests` and `mobile-ci` both pass.
- [ ] Push a throwaway commit that flips one expected `AttachResult` case in `RunnerTests.swift`; verify `runner-tests` goes red, `mobile-ci` goes red, the other five jobs stay green; revert.
- [ ] Confirm the PR is blocked from merge while red (branch protection on `mobile-ci`).
- [ ] Inspect the failing run's `RunnerTests.xcresult` artifact and verify it opens in Xcode.

Combines two orthogonal fixes that have each been deadlocked in their own PR (each blocked by the bug the *other* fixes). Shipping both in one PR so CI can go green in a single run without bypass-merging.

**Closes the deadlock between #4222 and #4224 — both will be closed in favor of this PR.**

## Changes

### 1. Revert #4128 — drop the broken iOS Runner Tests lane

The lane has been red on every PR (and on \`main\` itself) since #4128 merged. Root cause: an SPM workspace-load race in Xcode 26.x's \`IDESPMWorkspaceDelegate.dependencyPackagesDidUpdate\` that crashes \`xcodebuild\` with \`count of array (53) differs from count of index set (52)\` before any test executes.

Reproduced on both Xcode 26.3 (the original pin) and 26.2 (verified on a closed experimental PR — same crash, same stack frames). A 16.x downgrade isn't viable: \`pro_video_editor 1.15.0\`'s \`CompositionBuilder.swift\` references \`AVVideoCompositionLayerInstruction.Configuration\`, an iOS 26 SDK type that Swift type-checks at compile time.

Re-land #4128 once Apple ships an Xcode 26.x without the SPM race (watch for 26.4) or once the \`macos-26-arm64\` runner image is available with a working Xcode. This loses the \`NostrBridgeAttestationPolicy\` regression gate in the meantime.

### 2. Restore \`PathProviderPlatform.instance\` in seed-media test \`tearDown\`

#4154 ("fix(test): re-enable Bucket E skipped tests #3137", commit \`5a525e7bf\`) removed \`@Tags(['skip_very_good_optimization'])\` from \`mobile/test/services/seed_media_preload_service_test.dart\`, putting it back into the merged VGV optimized-isolate run.

Closes #4223

## Summary

Reverts #4128. The new `iOS Runner Tests` lane has been red on every PR — and on `main` itself — since it merged. This unblocks the CI queue.

## Root cause

Xcode 26.x has an SPM workspace-load race in `IDESPMWorkspaceDelegate.dependencyPackagesDidUpdate` that crashes `xcodebuild` with `count of array (53) differs from count of index set (52)` before any test executes. The same `IDEGroup insertGroupSubitems:atIndexes:context:` stack frames appear on every run.

Verified on both versions available on `macos-15-arm64`:

- Apple ships an Xcode 26.x without the SPM race (watch for 26.4), or

title: fix(perf): cap profile-tab thumbnail decode size to keep ImageCache from thrashing
body:
## Summary

- Adds a `memCacheWidth: 400` constraint to `ProfileTabThumbnail`'s `VineCachedImage`. The cap mirrors the existing pattern in `video_notification_row.dart` and is sized for 3-column phone tiles at 3.2× pixel ratio.
- Without it, `cached_network_image` decodes thumbnails at native CDN resolution (~3 MB each); a 50+ tile profile grid overflows Flutter's default `ImageCache` budget, thrashes the cache, and stalls first paint by ~1s.
- Single-file production change; benefits every profile tab grid that shares the widget (videos / liked / reposts / saved / collabs / comments).

Surfaced by @hm21 on [PR #4182 review](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/4182#pullrequestreview-4257513564).

Closes #4190.

## Why this scope

The two related perf issues — #3603 (de-dup in `build()`) and #3605 (`context.watch` on `BackgroundPublishBloc`) — only affect the **own-profile-with-active-uploads** path. The reviewer's repro is opening *another user's* profile, where `isOwnProfile=false` makes both no-ops. The dominant cost in that path is image decode + `ImageCache` thrash on first paint of the 50-event relay burst, which this PR addresses directly. Both related issues remain open for their assignees.

If QA still observes residual jank after this lands, the next layer to look at is the provider-side cascade in `profile_feed_provider.dart` — `_relayVideosSnapshot()` re-sorts the bucket on every relay tick (`video_event_service.dart:886-887`) and `filterVideoList` does two O(N) passes per emit (`video_event_service.dart:633-697`). That refactor needs its own scoping and is intentionally out of scope here.

- [x] `flutter test test/widgets/profile/profile_tab_thumbnail_test.dart` — 9 / 9 pass (8 existing + 1 new pinning `memCacheWidth == 400` and `memCacheHeight == null` so `BoxFit.cover` still scales proportionally).

title: fix(perf): cache BlurhashDisplay decode future across rebuilds
body:
## Description

`BlurhashDisplay` constructed a fresh `_createImageFromPixels(...)` future inside its `build()` method. Each parent rebuild created a new `Future` (different identity), so `FutureBuilder` treated it as a fresh request and re-showed the gradient fallback while the new decode completed. On a 50+ tile profile grid churning under `BackgroundPublishBloc` upload-progress emissions (tracked in #3605), this multiplied into visible flicker across the whole grid plus redundant `decodeImageFromPixels` calls per visible tile.

This was surfaced on low-end Android in @hm21's [review of PR #4191](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/4191#pullrequestreview-4257933582), as one of three layers of residual jank that PR's `memCacheWidth` cap didn't address.

### Fix

Cache the decode future in `State` so its identity stays stable across rebuilds, and recompute it only when `blurhash` / `contentType` actually change:

- New `Future<ui.Image?>? _imageFuture` field on `_BlurhashDisplayState`.
- `_decodeBlurhash()` now constructs the future once when new `BlurhashData` arrives, alongside `_blurhashData`, inside the existing `setState`.
- `build()` reads `_imageFuture` instead of constructing a new one each call.

Single-file production change (+12 / -6). Test added pinning the new invariant.

**Related Issue:** Closes #4196

## Type of Change

- [x] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter test test/widgets/profile/profile_tab_thumbnail_test.dart test/widgets/video_thumbnail_widget_test.dart` — 20/20 pass (existing tests that exercise `BlurhashDisplay` via its callers).

## Related (not addressed here)

title: feat(popular): add time-period filter to Explore → Popular tab
body:
Closes #4148

## Description

Adds a 5-chip time-period filter to the Explore → Popular tab, deep-linkable via `?period=…` query param.

**The chips:** Right Now · Today · This Week · This Month · All Time

- **Right Now** keeps the current behavior — `/api/videos?sort=watching` (24h CDN view count, no age decay).
- **Today / This Week / This Month / All Time** route through funnelcake's `/api/leaderboard/videos?period=…` endpoint (newly wired into the funnelcake client).

**Architecture** (per `.claude/rules/architecture.md`):
- UI chip taps push URL changes (`context.go('/explore/tab/popular?period=<slug>')`)
- `ExploreScreen.didChangeDependencies` syncs `?period=` from `GoRouterState` into a Riverpod `StateProvider<LeaderboardPeriod?>` (post-frame to avoid build-phase writes)
- `popularVideosFeedProvider` watches the StateProvider; period flip triggers a fresh `_loadFirstPage`
- `VideosRepository.getPopularVideos({period: ...})` dispatches to `/api/leaderboard/videos` when period is set, falls through to existing watching/NIP-50 path when null
- A sealed `_PopularCursor` (timestamp vs offset) keeps pagination semantics straight across the two paths

**URL format:**
- `/explore/tab/popular` — Right Now (default)
- `/explore/tab/popular?period=today|week|month|alltime` — windowed leaderboard

`fromUrlSlug` accepts both `today` and `day` for back-compat; the canonical emit is always `today` for shareability.

**l10n:** 6 new keys (label + 5 chip names) added to `app_en.arb` only; allowlisted in `_knownUntranslatedDebt` in `arb_consistency_test.dart`. Translations land in a follow-up locale-pass PR.

## What's NOT in this PR

A **New / Classics** content axis on the Popular tab is intentionally **out of scope**. The combination `Classics × {Today,Week,Month,All Time}` is server-blocked: `/api/leaderboard/videos` silently ignores unknown query params (verified by live probe — `?platform=vine` returns identical bytes to the bare query) and the response items don't include a `platform` field at all, so client-side filtering also isn't possible.

The funnelcake-side ask is to:
1. Add `platform=` query support to `/api/leaderboard/videos` (matching `/api/videos`)
2. Include `platform` in the leaderboard response items

Once that ships, the kind axis can land as a small follow-up PR (one `popularKindProvider`, one chip row, no new endpoint plumbing).

`Right Now × Classics` works today via the existing `?sort=watching&platform=vine` combo and could ship in this PR — but it'd be a half-feature ("kind axis only available on Right Now") with confusing UX, so we're holding the entire kind axis until the server work lands.

## Test plan

Automated:
- Funnelcake client: 10 new tests covering URL construction, all 4 period wire values, offset pagination, response edge cases, error paths
- Repository: 5 new tests covering period dispatch, offset propagation, no-NIP-50-fallback semantics, period-keyed cache, watching-path regression
- Provider: 3 new tests covering period propagation, default null behavior, rebuild-on-flip
- Widget (`PopularFilterBar`): 6 tests covering chip rendering, selected state, URL push, urlSlug-vs-wireValue distinction, Right Now clears `?period=`
- Widget (`PopularVideosTab`): 1 smoke test that the filter bar renders above the grid
- Screen (URL → provider sync): 5 tests covering ?period=week, today-slug back-compat, bare URL clears, invalid value, no-GoRouter no-op
- l10n consistency: existing test extended with the 6 new keys
- **Full mobile suite**: 8344 pass / 400 skip / 0 fail post-rebase

Manual (still needed before merge):
- [ ] Tap each chip on a real device, verify URL updates and grid refreshes
- [ ] Deep-link `/explore/tab/popular?period=week` from cold start, verify correct chip is selected and grid loads
- [ ] Background the app for 10s, return — verify selected chip survives
- [ ] Verify scroll-to-hide animation works for the new chip row alongside the existing trending hashtags row
- [ ] Pull-to-refresh on each window — confirm correct endpoint is hit (network logs)
- [ ] Test with `flutter run` in different system text scales — chip row should grow with text, not clip

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] ❌ Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] 🧹 Code refactor
- [ ] ✅ Build configuration change
- [ ] 📝 Documentation
- [ ] 🗑️ Chore

## Notes

- Implementation plan is committed at `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-08-popular-tab-time-period-filter.md` for future maintainers.

title: fix(profile): preserve arbitrary Kind 0 fields across profile edits
body:
## Summary

Closes #4175.

Editing a profile silently dropped any Kind 0 field the typed `UserProfile` model didn't know about — `lud16`, `lud06`, `website`, `bot`, NIP-39 `i` tags, custom client keys, future NIP additions. PR #4022 patched the symptom for `nip05` only; this PR generalizes the fix to every field.

## What changes

### Two-layer fix

1. **`ProfileRepository.saveProfileEvent` now seeds from the freshest relay Kind 0** before composing the new event content. Relay events round-trip through `UserProfile.fromNostrEvent`, which preserves the full content as `rawData` — so unknown fields survive byte-identical. Falls back to `currentProfile` on relay timeout/failure.
2. **`UserProfile.fromUserProfileFound` now mirrors the typed REST fields into `rawData`** (defense-in-depth — kicks in when the relay fetch fails). The Funnelcake REST API does not expose the raw Kind 0 JSON, so unknown fields can only be recovered via the relay seed.

### Merge contract

The new `saveProfileEvent` builds the published content from a copy of `seed.rawData`, then applies a small set of explicit deltas:

- **Editable fields** (`display_name`, `about`, `picture`, `banner`): caller's value wins. Empty/null **removes the key** — the form is pre-populated from the seed, so an empty submit is treated as an explicit clear.
- **`nip05`**: keeps the race-protected clear semantics from #4022 — only removed when `clearNip05: true`.
- **Every other key**: passes through from the seed untouched.

Also drops the previous behavior of writing explicit `null` for unset editable fields; those keys are now omitted entirely. Semantically equivalent on all major Nostr clients, and consistent with how unknown-field preservation works (no key === unset).

## Why this matters

A divine-mobile user who edits their bio in our app no longer silently rewrites their Kind 0 in a way that erases work done in any other client (Damus, Amethyst, Primal, etc.). Lightning zaps via `lud16` keep working. NIP-39 identity proofs survive. Future NIPs that we don't yet model survive automatically.

## Tests

The load-bearing invariant is pinned by a new test in `profile_repository_test.dart`:

> "preserves arbitrary unknown fields when seeded from a relay-fetched Kind 0"

The seed has `bot`, `i`, `lud16`, `lud06`, `website`, and a `weird_future_field`. Editing only `display_name` produces a published event whose every non-`display_name` key is byte-identical to the seed.

Other new tests:
- `falls back to currentProfile when relay seed fetch fails`
- `mirrors typed REST fields into rawData` (`user_profile_test.dart`)
- `omits null typed fields from rawData` (`user_profile_test.dart`)

Existing `saveProfileEvent` tests were updated for the new omit-empty-keys contract. The #4022 nip05 preservation regression test was kept intact.

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter test` in `mobile/packages/models` — 103 passing
- [x] `flutter test` in `mobile/packages/profile_repository` — 195 passing
- [x] `flutter test mobile/test/blocs/profile_editor/` — 71 passing
- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` from `mobile/` — clean
- [ ] Manual: log in as a user with `lud16` set in another client; edit display_name in divine-mobile; inspect published Kind 0 via `wss://relay.divine.video` — confirm `lud16` is present.

## Out of scope

- Funnelcake REST returning the raw Kind 0 event JSON — would let the typed REST factory carry unknown fields too. Track in `divine-funnelcake`. Until then, the relay seed step is the only path that preserves unknown fields.
- Same `rawData`-loss pattern on other replaceable kinds (kind 3 follow lists, kind 10002 relay lists, kind 10000 mute lists). Worth a survey but not in this PR.

title: fix(deep-link): hit Funnelcake REST before relays for /video/<id>
body:
Closes #4178

## Summary

- Cold-start `divine.video/video/<sha256>` deep-links were stuck behind a generic spinner for 60s+ before rendering. Reorders `fetchVideoWithStatsForRouteId` to local cache → Funnelcake REST → relay (each capped by a 3s timeout), so the canonical REST source answers first instead of running last after two relay round-trips that wait for EOSE from disconnected relays.
- Swaps the deep-link loading state from a generic Material `CircularProgressIndicator` to `BrandedLoadingIndicator` (matches the rest of the app).

## Why this was slow

`_VideoRouteCandidate.parse` treats a 64-char hex routeId as **both** an event id and a stable id. The previous flow ran:

1. `_nostrClient.queryEvents([Filter(ids:[hash], …)])` — never matches for Blossom-hashed share URLs (kind 34236 event ids are computed differently, the URL hash is the d-tag).
2. `_nostrClient.queryEvents([Filter(d:[hash], …)])` — may match.
3. Funnelcake REST.

`NostrClient.queryEvents` waits for EOSE from every relay in the pool with a 5s default timeout, and any relay still mid-connect during cold start blocks the whole batch. The on-relay-ready retry in `VideoDetailScreen` then re-runs the entire sequence on first relay connection. Worst case: ~5s + ~5s + Funnelcake + relay-ready wait + ~5s + ~5s + Funnelcake = comfortably 60s.

REST is now first because it answers in <1s without waiting on relay state and is the canonical source for divine.video share URLs. Relay is kept as a fallback so events that only live on a user's personal relay still resolve.

title: feat(dm): self-wrap-only recovery for sentPartial sends
body:
## Description

Closes #4102 — the technical-debt follow-up to PR #3908.

When a NIP-17 send delivers to the recipient but the sender's
self-addressed gift wrap fails to publish, `ConversationBloc` emits
`SendStatus.sentPartial`. Tapping Retry on the SnackBar previously
redispatched the full `ConversationMessageSent` path, which republished
the recipient gift wrap and double-delivered the message. NIP-17 self
wraps are independent of recipient wraps — only the missing self wrap
needs to land on retry, never the recipient one. This PR adds the
self-wrap-only recovery primitive plus the matching BLoC event and
SnackBar wiring so Retry-on-`sentPartial` republishes only the sender's
gift wrap, leaving recipients untouched.

**Related Issue:** Closes #4102 (follow-up to #3908)

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

## Changes

**`NIP17MessageService` (`packages/dm_repository`)**
- New `publishSelfWrap({required Event rumorEvent})`: builds + publishes
  only the sender self-addressed gift wrap for a pre-existing rumor,
  sharing the underlying self-wrap helper with `sendRumor` so the two
  paths agree on null-builder, publish-failure, and exception handling.

**`DmRepository.recoverSelfWrap(rumorId)`**
- Looks up the queue row by `rumorId`, rebuilds the rumor from
  `rumor_event_json` (preserving the receiver-side dedup key), publishes
  via `publishSelfWrap`, then deletes the row on success or marks
  `self_wrap_status: failed` for the next retry sweep.
- Idempotent against an already-sent row, defends against missing rows,
  foreign-owner rows (cross-account safety), corrupted rumor JSON, and a
  missing queue DAO.

**`DmRepository.sendGroupMessage`**
- Refactored to enqueue a queue row per recipient, mirroring
  `sendMessage`, and to write per-recipient outcomes inside the same
  transaction as the local message persist. This is what lets group
  recovery scope to only the affected successful recipient sends — the
  prior implementation shared a single send path with no queue rows, so
  partial group deliveries had nowhere to look up the rumor for replay.

**`ConversationState`**
- New `PartialSend({required List<String> rumorIds})` carries the
  per-recipient rumor ids whose self-wrap failed.
- `lastPartialSend` lives alongside `lastFailedSend` with its own clear
  flag in `copyWith`. The two states drive different recovery paths
  (full resend vs self-wrap-only), so they're tracked independently.

**`ConversationBloc`**
- On `sentPartial`, populates `lastPartialSend` (not `lastFailedSend`)
  with the rumor ids of the partial-self results.
- New `ConversationSelfWrapRecoveryRequested(rumorIds)` event with a
  `sequential()` transformer (same as `ConversationMessageSent`).
- The handler loops `recoverSelfWrap` per id, aggregates outcomes, and
  reduces `lastPartialSend.rumorIds` to only the still-failing ids so a
  second Retry tap targets exactly those.
- Removes the obsolete "TODO #3909" tradeoff comment block — the
  principled fix it described is now in place.

**`ConversationView`**
- `_onSendOutcome`'s SnackBar action branches on `sendStatus`:
  `sentPartial` dispatches `ConversationSelfWrapRecoveryRequested`,
  `failed` keeps dispatching `ConversationMessageSent`.

**l10n**
- No new keys. The existing `dmSendPartialMessage` and
  `dmSendFailedRetry` already exist in all 17 locales (added by PR
  #3908).

## Test plan

Automated:
- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — clean.
- [x] `dart format` — no changes.
- [x] `mobile/packages/dm_repository` 217/217 passing (12 new tests:
  5 `publishSelfWrap`, 5 `sendGroupMessage` queue, 7 `recoverSelfWrap`).
- [x] `mobile/test/blocs/dm` + `mobile/test/screens/inbox` 311/311
  passing (4 new self-wrap recovery scenarios + 3 new event-equality
  tests + 3 new state-shape tests + 1 new view-test for retry-dispatch).

Pinning contracts added:
- `recoverSelfWrap` never publishes a recipient wrap (verified via
  `verifyNever(messageService.sendRumor(...))` and
  `verifyNever(messageService.sendPrivateMessage(...))` after recovery).
- `ConversationSelfWrapRecoveryRequested` handler never calls
  `dmRepository.sendMessage` or `sendGroupMessage`.
- View test: tapping Retry on the partial-delivery SnackBar dispatches
  `ConversationSelfWrapRecoveryRequested` (not
  `ConversationMessageSent`).

Manual verification (please confirm during review):
- [ ] Force a self-wrap publish failure on a 1:1 send (e.g. block the
  second `publishEvent` round in a debug build) → SnackBar shows the
  partial-delivery copy → Retry resyncs the self-wrap without sending
  a second bubble to the recipient.
- [ ] Same for a group send where one of the per-recipient self-wraps
  fails → only that one rumor's self-wrap is republished on Retry.
- [ ] After a successful recovery, leave + re-enter the conversation —
  the `outgoing_dms` row for that rumor should be gone.

## Investigation notes

The plan in `tasks/lessons.md` shape, including the architectural
choice to enqueue group sends per-recipient (so partial group recovery
has a queue-row source of truth), was captured in /plan output for
#4102 prior to implementation.

title: fix(profile): wire avatar upload through bytes API on web (#3887)
body:
## Description

Avatar upload was a no-op on Flutter web. `image_picker` hands back a
`blob:` URL on web, and `dart:io File(blob:…).readAsBytes()` throws
on the first I/O call. PR #3880 made the failure classifier friendlier
but still hid the underlying break behind the generic fallback
snackbar. The desktop picker branch was also broken on web because
`defaultTargetPlatform` reports the host OS in a desktop browser, so
file_selector ran against a blob URL too.

This wires the avatar upload through a bytes path on web while
leaving the native flow unchanged.

**Related Issue:** Closes #3887

### What changed

- **`BlossomUploadService`** gains `uploadImageBytes(bytes, filename,
  …)` for callers that already hold image bytes (i.e. web). The
  internal upload helpers (`_uploadToServer`,
  `_uploadToServerResumable`, `_uploadChunks`,
  `_uploadToServerLegacyFallback`) now take an `_UploadSource`
  abstraction so file (streaming) and bytes (in-memory) sources share
  the same Blossom BUD-01 plumbing — including the resumable chunked
  upload path. `uploadImage(File)`, `uploadVideo(File)`,
  `uploadAudio(File)`, and `uploadBugReport(File)` keep their
  signatures, just wrap the file in `_FileUploadSource` internally.
  Native callers still get the platform-channel EXIF stripper.

- **`ImageMetadataStripper`** gains `stripMetadataBytes(bytes,
  filename)` — pure-Dart EXIF removal that mirrors
  `stripMetadataInPlace`'s rename rule (PNG keeps its extension;
  everything that re-encodes to JPEG switches to `.jpg`). Native code
  keeps using `stripMetadataInPlace` for the hardware-accelerated
  platform stripper.

- **`profile_setup_screen`** picks an `XFile`, reads the bytes on web,
  and uploads via `uploadImageBytes`. Native picks keep the `dart:io
  File` flow. `_isDesktopPlatform()` now short-circuits to `false` on
  web so a Mac/Linux browser stops routing through `file_selector`.
  The stop-gap `kIsWeb` "not supported" snackbar from PR #3880 is
  removed.

## Description

`videoListsEqual` used `==` to compare `VideoEvent` instances, but `VideoEvent.==` only checks `id`. After background Nostr enrichment merged a blurhash into a video, the enriched list compared as "equal" to the existing state, so no state update was emitted and widgets never rebuilt.

- `BlurhashService._isValidBlurhash`: removed the incorrect `L`-prefix requirement because valid blurhashes can start with any base83 character

## Summary

PR 2 of 3 for #3795 (Liz's prescribed sequence: telemetry → retry → classification tightening).

- Adds `isRetryable()` and `retryConsume()` helpers to `InviteErrorUtils` -- classifies `temporary` and `authFailure` errors as retryable, retries up to 3x with 2s delay

title: fix(notifications): clear unread badge by syncing Riverpod cache on inbox open
body:
## Summary

- Fixes #4144 (notification badge count not clearing) — duplicate of #4048
- Supersedes #4149 (close that PR after this lands)
- Two-bug fix: an `_onStarted` / `_onMarkAllRead` ordering race in the BLoC, plus a BLoC ↔ Riverpod cache desync that left the bottom-nav badge stale until the 5-min auto-refresh

## Why

The notifications subsystem is mid-migration to BLoC, but the bottom-nav badge and inbox segmented-toggle count are still driven by the legacy `relayNotificationsProvider` (Riverpod) cache. Opening the inbox marks-read in the BLoC's `NotificationRepository` — both stacks POST to the same server endpoint, but neither propagates to the other's in-memory cache, so the badge stays unread until Riverpod's 5-min auto-refresh fires. Users perceive this as "notifications not going away."

The pre-existing PR #4149 attempted a tactical bridge by calling `relayNotificationsProvider.notifier.markAllAsRead()` from `NotificationsView.initState`. The reviewer (@NotThatKindOfDrLiz) blocked it on three points: a duplicated weaker `_onStarted` mark-read that bypassed the rollback path #4034 added, fan-out across the five `NotificationsView` tabs mounted by `TabBarView`, and missing test coverage of the side effect. This PR addresses all three.

## What changed

**`mobile/lib/notifications/bloc/notification_feed_bloc.dart`**
- `_onStarted` re-dispatches `NotificationFeedMarkAllRead` after the loaded state is emitted, instead of inlining a weaker mark-read. The existing `_onMarkAllRead` rollback / `addError` path runs uniformly.

**`mobile/lib/notifications/view/inbox_notifications_page.dart`** and **`notifications_page.dart`**
- Both pages now own a single Riverpod sync via `ref.listenManual` with `fireImmediately: true`, guarded by a `_relaySynced` one-shot flag plus an unread-check on the resolved provider state. Fires exactly once per page open whether the provider is warm (already loaded by the bottom nav) or cold-starting.
- Standalone `NotificationsPage` is converted from `ConsumerWidget` to `ConsumerStatefulWidget`. `_InboxNotificationsScaffold` is converted from `StatefulWidget` to `ConsumerStatefulWidget`.

**`mobile/lib/notifications/view/notifications_view.dart`**
- Adds a `mounted` guard inside the post-frame callback. Note: the per-`NotificationsView` Riverpod call from PR #4149's diff is intentionally absent here — the side effect lives at the page level so it doesn't fan out across the five `TabBarView` children.

## Tests

- BLoC tests: assert `_notificationRepository.markAllAsRead()` is called once after `NotificationFeedStarted` with unread items, and `verifyNever` when the loaded page is already all-read. Existing `isFollowingBack` derivation test updated for the additional optimistic-mark-read state. Default `markAllAsRead` stub added to the parent `setUp` so existing `NotificationFeedStarted` tests don't regress.
- New `mobile/test/notifications/view/inbox_notifications_page_test.dart`: verifies the Riverpod side effect fires exactly once per inbox open, not at all when nothing is unread, and stays at one call after swiping through all five filter tabs.
- Extended `notifications_page_test.dart` with parallel assertions for the standalone `/notifications/:index` route.

- [ ] CI: build / Analyze / Tests / Format / Generated Files

## Out of scope (followup)

The dual-stack architecture itself remains. The proper destination — promote `NotificationRepository.watchUnreadCount()` to a stream and add a `NotificationBadgeCubit` mirroring `DmUnreadCountCubit` — is captured in `mobile/docs/brainstorm/2026-05-09-issue4144-notification-badge-desync-brainstorm.md` as Approach C. ## Description

Phase 1 emergency block for #3359 — strips the user's nsec from the
Keycast OAuth registration wire on both channels:

- `body['nsec']` field in `POST /api/headless/register`
- `<random>.<nsec1...>` suffix embedded in the PKCE `code_verifier`
  (later POSTed as `code_verifier` to `/api/oauth/token`)

The fix removes the parameters from the `keycast_flutter` package API
entirely so a future caller cannot re-introduce the leak. A POSIX-grep
CI guard locks the rule in.

**Related Issue:** Closes #3359

**Cross-repo coordination:** divinevideo/keycast#197 tracks the

title: ci(ios): add QA PR build slots
body:
Closes #3424

Revives the work from #3440 as a fresh draft PR after reverting the original rollout in #3719.

## Current status

This PR is intentionally back in **draft**. The original merge of #3440 broke Codemagic and had to be reverted. This PR is a straight replay of that original diff onto current `main` so the work can be picked up again deliberately, not merged as-is.

## What broke in the original rollout

Two things made the original rollout unsafe:

1. **`codemagic.yaml` was changed directly**
   - The PR added a new `ios-qa-pr-build` workflow and new QA-slot assumptions around env vars, signing, and distribution.
   - Because `codemagic.yaml` is global CI/CD config, mistakes there can break existing Codemagic behavior immediately, even if app code is fine.

2. **The GitHub allocator workflow tried to trigger Codemagic without guaranteed credentials**
   - The failing run on April 30, 2026 hit a `401` from the Codemagic build trigger.
   - In that run, `CODEMAGIC_APP_ID` and `CODEMAGIC_API_TOKEN` were empty in the workflow environment.
   - The workflow treated that as a hard failure instead of degrading safely, so PR checks went red.

## Root cause

The main problem was not the app identity wiring itself. The problem was that live infra automation was merged before its operational prerequisites were reliably present, and the automation did not fail closed when those prerequisites were missing.

More concretely:
- external setup was still incomplete
- the workflow was active enough to execute anyway
- missing Codemagic credentials produced a hard failure instead of a safe skip/queue state
- too many surfaces were bundled into one PR at once:
  - app identity wiring
  - GitHub Actions allocator
  - Python allocator library/tests
  - Codemagic config
  - docs/specs

## What needs to happen before this can merge again

This PR should be treated as source material for a safer re-rollout, not as merge-ready work.

Recommended rollout plan:

1. **Fail closed when secrets/config are missing**
   - Any automation that triggers external systems must check for required secrets first.
   - If secrets are absent, it should skip or queue, not fail.

2. **Split the rollout into smaller PRs**
   - docs/spec only
   - pure allocator library + tests
   - workflow skeleton that only comments/labels and does not trigger Codemagic
   - Codemagic integration only after secrets and env are confirmed
   - app-side identity wiring only if still needed

3. **Treat `codemagic.yaml` as high-risk infra**
   - Review it separately from normal app code.
   - Require a rollback path before merging.

4. **Gate new automation behind explicit opt-in**
   - Example: require a label like `needs-ios-qa` before allocator/build logic runs.
   - Do not auto-run new infra on every trusted PR on day one.

5. **Add explicit missing-prerequisite handling**
   - missing Codemagic credentials
   - missing Firebase config
   - missing repo variables
   - external API 401/403

6. **Prove the workflow in a throwaway PR before rollout**
   - Validate it with real repo secrets/variables in place.
   - Do not use production PR traffic as the first real test.

7. **Keep external setup separate from active automation**
   - If Chunk 0 setup is incomplete, the workflow should remain inert.
   - Scaffolded but disabled is safer than enabled but half-provisioned.

## Notes for whoever picks this up

- This branch currently exists so the original work is preserved and reviewable.
- It should likely be split or partially reimplemented rather than merged intact.
- #3719 reverted the original merge after it broke Codemagic builds.
- #3721 added a temporary guard so the broken allocator workflow would stop hard-failing while the revert landed.

## Summary

This draft PR is here so the iOS QA slot work can be resumed safely. It is **not** a signal that the original rollout shape was sound. The next attempt should be narrower, safer by default, and validated against real secrets/config before merge.

title: feat(nostr): reliable publish primitives + NIP-09 deletion reference migration
body:
Closes #3178

First PR in an 8-PR series to make every Nostr publish in divine-mobile durable. See `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-20-reliable-nostr-publish-README.md` for the full plan.

## Summary

- Adds `PublishOutcome`, `NostrClient.publishEventAwaitOk`, `NostrClient.publishEventWithRetry` (bounded exponential backoff, retries only transient relays per NIP-01) — the primitives every follow-up PR uses.
- Adds `PublishResultMapper` so every future service migration maps outcome → user feedback uniformly (success / retryable error / permanent reject with reason).
- Extends `NostrClientStatisticsObserver` with `onPublishOutcome` for per-attempt publish telemetry.
- Migrates `ContentDeletionService` as the reference implementation; `_deleteVideo` in `share_video_menu.dart` now shows a retry-able snackbar on transient failure.
- **Contract change for deletion:** the previous "save locally even if publish fails" branch is removed. Durable deletion now requires at least one relay accept — fixes the ghost-delete bug where the UI believed content was deleted while every other client could still see it.
- Merges cleanly with PR #3117's \`DeleteFailureKind\` localization work — \`DeleteResult\` now carries both \`failureKind\` (pre-publish) and \`outcome\`/\`feedback\` (post-publish).

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter test mobile/test/services/content_deletion_service_test.dart` — all 10 existing tests pass against the new `publishEventWithRetry` contract.
- [x] `flutter test mobile/test/unit/services/content_deletion_service_reliability_test.dart` — 3 new tests (success / transient / permanent reject).
- [x] `flutter test mobile/packages/nostr_sdk` — 241+ tests including 7 `PublishOutcome` + 5 `RelayPool.sendAwaitOk` tests.
- [x] `flutter test mobile/packages/nostr_client` — 11 new tests (5 `RetryPolicy` + 6 `PublishResultMapper`).
- [x] `flutter analyze` clean on all changed files.
- [ ] Manually delete a video on a staging relay that drops OK frames — expect retry snackbar with Retry action.
- [ ] Manually delete on a relay that returns \`blocked:\` — expect non-retryable snackbar with the reason.

## Architecture

Four layers, no new top-level packages:

1. **`nostr_sdk/RelayPool`** extends the existing NIP-20 OK handler (previously AUTH-only at `relay_pool.dart:369`) to also resolve pending publishes via per-event completers. New `sendAwaitOk` returns once every target relay has accepted/rejected or the 15s timeout elapses.
2. **`nostr_sdk/Nostr.sendEventAwaitOk`** signs and calls the pool wrapper, returning `PublishOutcome`.
3. **`nostr_client/NostrClient.publishEventAwaitOk`** preserves the existing optimistic-cache + relay-health + cache-rollback behavior. `publishEventWithRetry` wraps it with a `RetryPolicy` (default: 3 attempts, 2s base delay doubled each retry, capped at 30s, 15s per-attempt timeout) and retries only `outcome.transientRelays`.
4. **`nostr_client/PublishResultMapper`** turns a `PublishOutcome` into `PublishUserFeedback{severity, messageKey, retryable, firstRejectionReason}` so UI layers have a single source of truth.

## Out of scope for this PR

The 28 remaining publish call sites (video publish, social graph, DMs, mutes, bookmarks, account deletion, …) migrate in PRs 2–7, and fire-and-forget publishes are annotated in PR 8. Each follow-up plan is in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-20-reliable-nostr-publish-pr*.md`.

body:
## Description

Add a persistent SQLite feed cache to the home and latest feeds, enabling instant video display on cold start via a stale-while-revalidate strategy. Previously, every app launch required a network round-trip before any videos appeared. Now, the last successful feed response is persisted to a Drift `feed_cache` table and served immediately on next launch, while a background revalidation fetches fresh data for the subsequent open.

This replaces the previous `HomeFeedCache` (SharedPreferences) approach which had a stale-data problem: it was written once on initial Funnelcake fetch but never updated by background revalidation, because the DB cache path returned `HomeFeedResult` without `rawResponseBody`. The new approach keeps caching entirely in the repository layer where revalidation can update it directly.

### How it works

**Write path:** When a feed is fetched (from Funnelcake API or Nostr relay fallback), the response is serialized and stored in the `feed_cache` table keyed by feed mode (`"home"`, `"latest"`). Popular mode is excluded (being removed in #2344).

**Read path (cold start):**
1. Check in-memory cache (empty on cold start)
2. Check SQLite DB cache → if found, return cached videos immediately and fire a background revalidation
3. If no cache, fall through to network fetch as before

**Revalidation:** Runs in background (`unawaited`), hits the same Funnelcake API → relay waterfall, and updates both in-memory and DB caches. The BLoC does NOT re-emit after revalidation — fresh data appears on the next user interaction (mode switch, pull-to-refresh, app resume, follow list change). This avoids unexpected UI jank during active scrolling.

### Layers touched

- **Data layer (`db_client`):** New `feed_cache` table with `FeedCacheDao` for CRUD operations. Uses Drift's `DO UPDATE` for upsert semantics.
- **Repository layer (`videos_repository`):** New `_readFeedFromDb` / `_writeFeedToDb` / `_parseCachedFeedBody` helpers. New `_revalidateHomeFeed` / `_revalidateLatestFeed` background methods. Both Funnelcake and relay responses are now persisted (relay goes through `VideoEvent → VideoStats → JSON`).
- **Model layer (`models`):** `VideoStats.toJson()` for serialization. New `VideoStats.fromVideoEvent()` factory so relay-fetched `VideoEvent` objects can be converted to the same `VideoStats` JSON format the cache expects.
- **BLoC layer:** Removed `HomeFeedCache` (SharedPreferences) and its `serveCachedHomeFeed` / `_cacheServed` machinery — superseded by the repository DB cache which is properly updated by revalidation.

### Key design decisions

1. **Stale-while-revalidate over cache-then-network:** The BLoC emits cached data once and does not auto-refresh the UI when revalidation completes. This prevents feed "jumps" mid-scroll but means the user sees data from the previous session until they interact.
2. **Two serialization paths:** Funnelcake responses are stored as raw `response.body` (preserves original format). Relay responses go through `VideoEvent → VideoStats → JSON` since there's no raw body to cache.
3. **Feed key-based storage:** Each feed mode gets its own DB row (`"home"`, `"latest"`). `clearFeedCache()` can clear one or all.
4. **No TTL / max-age on DB cache:** Staleness is handled by always revalidating in background. If the app is killed before revalidation completes, the next open retries.
5. **Removed SharedPreferences cache:** The previous `HomeFeedCache` was never updated after the initial write because the DB cache read path didn't propagate `rawResponseBody`. Rather than fix that plumbing, we consolidated caching in the repository layer where revalidation has direct access.

### What this does NOT change

- The in-memory `InMemoryFeedCache` for instant mode switching is untouched.
- No changes to pagination (only initial page is cached).

## Type of Change

Closes #2313

title: test(apps): add E2E coverage for iOS frame attestation hop
body:
## Summary

Closes #4120 — follow-up to PR #3979 (iOS per-frame origin attestation).

The existing tests for the frame-attestation channel stop at the
`@visibleForTesting onAttestedEventHandlerReady` seam: widget tests
inject synthetic `Map<String, dynamic>` events into Dart, and Swift
unit tests pin the dictionary shape and policy in isolation. **Nothing
exercises the live `WKScriptMessage → FrameAttestingScriptMessageHandler
→ FlutterEventSink → EventChannel → broadcast stream → _handleAttestedEvent`
hop** — a channel-name typo, payload-key drift, or stream-lifecycle
regression on either side would silently degrade defence-in-depth to
nonce-only enforcement and leave every existing test green.

This PR adds one integration test that drives a real `WKWebView` against
a loopback HTTP fixture with both a main page and a same-origin iframe.

### What it covers

- A loopback `HttpServer.bind(InternetAddress.loopbackIPv4, 0)` serves
  two same-origin endpoints:
  - `GET /` → main HTML that polls for the pigeon-installed
    `window.divineSandboxBridge` alias and posts a request with the
    known `bridgeNonceOverride` once available.
  - `GET /iframe.html` → iframe HTML that calls
    `webkit.messageHandlers.divineSandboxBridge.postMessage(...)` raw,
    no nonce — exactly the attack vector PR #3979 closes.
- The main page contains `<iframe src=\"/iframe.html\">` so both frames
  are same-origin and `webkit.messageHandlers.divineSandboxBridge` is
  reachable from the iframe.
- `NostrAppSandboxScreen` is pumped with the existing seams
  (`javaScriptRunnerOverride`, `bridgeNonceOverride`,
  `currentUserPubkeyOverride`, `bridgeServiceOverride` for the positive
  case). No production-code change.
- A `_pumpUntil` helper polls the captured-scripts list with a 15 s
  cap (real time under `IntegrationTestWidgetsFlutterBinding`).
- `testWidgets` against `IntegrationTestWidgetsFlutterBinding`, runnable
  via `flutter test integration_test/apps/...`. Patrol's `PatrolBinding`
  conflicts with the auto-installed `IntegrationTestWidgetsFlutterBinding`
  under `flutter test`, so plain `testWidgets` is the right tool here —
  this test doesn't need patrol's native automation.

### Assertions

| Test | Asserts |
|------|---------|
| iframe-originated bridge traffic is rejected with `subframe_rejected` | Captured response for `id: 'frame'` contains `subframe_rejected` and not `\"success\":true`. |
| main-frame bridge traffic reaches the bridge service | Captured response for `id: 'main'` does not contain `subframe_rejected`, contains `\"success\":true`, and echoes the test pubkey. |

iOS-only: each `testWidgets` body early-returns on
`defaultTargetPlatform != TargetPlatform.iOS` since the native plugin
lives in the Runner target. Android per-frame attestation parity is
tracked in #4105.

### Approach selection

See the brainstorm doc bundled in this PR
(`mobile/docs/brainstorm/2026-05-08-issue4120-ios-frame-attestation-e2e-test-brainstorm.md`)
for the full comparison and the resolved-questions section. Approach A
(HTTP server + same-origin `<iframe src=...>`) was picked over
`srcdoc` (Approach B), bundled assets (Approach C), and a pure XCUITest
(Approach D) because it (1) matches the production threat model most
faithfully, (2) exercises the entire channel hop end-to-end, and (3)
requires no production-code or Xcode project changes.

## Test plan

- [x] `cd mobile && flutter analyze integration_test/apps/` — clean.
- [x] `cd mobile && dart format integration_test/apps/` — clean.
- [x] **iOS Simulator verification** — iPhone 17 Pro on iOS 26.4,
      Flutter 3.41.4. Three consecutive runs of
      `flutter test integration_test/apps/nostr_bridge_frame_attestation_test.dart -d <udid>`
      all green. Per-test wall time ~1–2 s (well inside the 15 s
      `_pumpUntil` cap).
- [x] **Loopback origin form resolved** — WKWebView preserves
      `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` verbatim through `loadRequest`. The
      fixture uses the literal IP form in both `launchUrl` and
      `allowedOrigins`; no rewrite to `localhost` was observed.
- [x] **Skip behavior** — early-return on `defaultTargetPlatform !=
      TargetPlatform.iOS` keeps the test inert on macOS / Android.

Resolved-questions section in the brainstorm doc (origin form, stubbed
bridge service, polling budget, ATS posture, harness choice) records
the same outcome.

title: chore: Gate Nostr side effects on session readiness
body:
## Description

Users could lose push registration on cold launch because auth could be ready before Nostr could sign yet.
This change separates identity readiness from Nostr readiness and makes signer-dependent work wait for the matching ready client.
That matters because push registration, notification preferences, and blocklist sync all publish Nostr events.

**Related Issue:** Closes #3929

## Type of Change

- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] ❌ Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] 🧹 Code refactor
- [ ] ✅ Build configuration change
- [ ] 📝 Documentation
- [ ] 🗑️ Chore

## Summary

Auth state now means the app knows who the user is.
It no longer means the Nostr client is ready to sign and publish.
The app now waits for an explicit ready session before running side effects that need the signer.

## What Changed

The flow now carries the ready pubkey and client together.
Work that publishes through Nostr rejects stale sessions and queues preferences until the matching session is ready.
Sign-out also runs outgoing push deregistration before signer teardown.

- Added `NostrSessionReadiness` and kept `isNostrReadyProvider` as a compatibility shim.
- Moved push registration, token refresh, preference publishing, push deregistration, and blocklist sync to ready-session or pre-teardown paths.
- Added warning-only wrappers so non-critical push publish failures do not escape async listeners.
- Added regression tests for cold launch, account switch, teardown ordering, queued preferences, and async error handling.

## Testing

I rebased onto latest `origin/main` and ran the full Flutter checks.
The analyzer found no issues, and the full test suite passed with 8,383 passing tests and 400 skipped tests.

- `git fetch https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile.git main:refs/remotes/origin/main && git rebase origin/main`
- `flutter analyze`
- `flutter test`

## Risks

The main risk is lifecycle ordering around sign-out and account switch.
The new tests cover the flows that could use a stale or placeholder Nostr client.
Identity-only listeners such as routing and Zendesk still use auth state.

title: fix(feed): hydrate views/loops on New feed via bulk stats
body:
## Summary
- `getNewVideos` was the only feed-fetch path that skipped `_hydrateVideosWithBulkStats`, so freshly published Nostr videos showed "0 loops" in the **New** feed even when Funnelcake's bulk-stats endpoint already reported view counts.
- The relay fallback path had the same gap.
- Run hydration on both paths and cache the hydrated result so subsequent fetches read the populated counts.

## Why
Reproduced on event `bc96ec17636e1df781d7522814c073dafaa615027cd78520ca719bf4ef3cff68`:
- `GET /api/videos/{id}/views` → `{"views":11,"unique_viewers":6}`
- `POST /api/videos/stats/bulk` → `{"views":14,"loops":7.67}`
- `GET /api/videos?sort=recent` → `loops:7, views:11`
- `GET /api/videos/{id}` → `stats` block has reactions/comments/reposts only, no `views`/`loops`

`VideoEvent.totalLoops = (originalLoops ?? 0) + parseInt(rawTags['views'] ?? '')`. For new videos, `originalLoops` is null (only set for archived Vine imports) and `rawTags['views']` only exists when a Funnelcake list payload included it or hydration filled it in. The New feed's path didn't run any hydration, so `totalLoops` evaluated to `0` despite real engagement on the bulk-stats endpoint.

Other feeds (`getHomeFeedVideos`, `getPopularVideos`, `getVideosByIds`, `fetchVideoWithStats*`) already call `_hydrateVideosWithBulkStats`. This brings `getNewVideos` in line.
